Mission Local reported that the mayor’s upzoning plan would no longer apply to buildings with three or more rent-controlled apartments. The amendment was expected to exempt at least 84,000 rental units in 11,700 buildings, along with any ground-floor retail beneath them. Two-unit buildings were not covered and remained in the plan.

The story also said the change responded to tenant concerns that upzoning could encourage demolition of older, rent-controlled housing. It reported that protecting those units should not affect the plan’s broader goal of creating capacity for 36,000 additional homes to meet the state mandate.
